title: Skill Library
subtitle: A curated set of mainstream Agent Skills that actually earn their place, grouped by purpose. Every entry ships a one-click install command. Our own open-source skills will join over time.

skills.name: find-skills
skills.tagline: The skill that lets your agent find other skills
skills.overview: Tell your agent «I want to do X» and it searches the skills.sh catalog, proposes the matching skill and its install command, then installs it only after you confirm. Solves the biggest gap: not knowing what skills exist.
features: Turns natural-language needs into skill searches
Covers the full skills.sh catalog
Shows the install command and waits for your confirmation
Works with Claude Code, Cursor, Codex and more
useCases: You want a capability but don't know a skill exists for it
Ramping up on a new stack and its best practices
Adding vertical capabilities to a project on demand
skills.bestFor: Install this one first — then you never have to memorize install commands.
skills.author: Vercel Labs

skills.name: skill-creator
skills.tagline: An official skill for authoring your own skills
skills.overview: Anthropic's official skill-authoring assistant: it interviews you to distill requirements, generates a well-formed SKILL.md and directory layout, and handles validation and packaging. The first stop for turning your workflow into a reusable skill.
features: Interview-style prompts that surface tacit knowledge
Generates standard SKILL.md and folder structure
Built-in validation and packaging
Follows official best-practice templates
useCases: Codifying team conventions into a skill
Persisting a repetitive personal workflow
Building and publishing an open-source skill
skills.bestFor: Anyone who wants «how I work» to become reusable agent capability.
skills.author: Anthropic

skills.name: Superpowers
skills.tagline: Gives agents «brainstorm → plan → test → build» discipline
skills.overview: Jesse Vincent's (obra) collection of engineering workflow skills: brainstorming, implementation plans, TDD, systematic debugging, requesting and receiving code review… It makes AI coding follow disciplined process instead of typing at full speed. The most-installed workflow pack on skills.sh.
features: Enforces «brainstorm, then plan, then code»
TDD: failing tests first, implementation second
Systematic debugging: reproduce → hypothesize → verify
Parallel subagents and code-review workflows
useCases: Tired of ten-thousand-line one-shot generations
Multi-day features that need context management
Aligning AI output with team engineering standards
skills.bestFor: Required reading if you use AI coding seriously.
skills.author: Jesse Vincent (obra)

skills.name: grill-me
skills.tagline: Let the agent grill your plan before you build it
skills.overview: Matt Pocock's skill: before any code, the agent fires question after question at your idea — surfacing vague requirements, hidden assumptions and unconsidered edge cases — and only lets you go once the plan holds up. Changing your mind before coding is the cheapest fix there is.
features: Interrogates the plan point by point
Forces requirements, boundaries and acceptance criteria to be explicit
Low-cost course correction before implementation
Great substitute for a review partner when solo
useCases: You're only 50% sure but itching to start
Self-checking a PRD or tech design
Rehearsing risky refactors and migrations
skills.bestFor: People who want AI to build the right thing, not just build the thing right.
skills.author: Matt Pocock

skills.name: frontend-design
skills.tagline: Anthropic's cure for AI-generated «template face» UIs
skills.overview: Anthropic's official frontend design skill: it requires the agent to commit to a distinct visual style, bold typography, restrained motion and high information density — targeting the unmistakable «made by AI» look.
features: Rejects the generic default-Tailwind face
Insists on design personality and site-wide coherence
Concrete rules for type pairing and layout rhythm
Motion only where it genuinely earns its place
useCases: Every AI-generated page looks the same
Landing pages and dashboards that need brand feel
Giving your agent an eye for design
skills.bestFor: Standard equipment for anyone building UIs with AI.
skills.author: Anthropic

skills.name: web-design-guidelines
skills.tagline: A design-standard physical for your interface
skills.overview: Vercel's interface-guidelines skill: hundreds of actionable rules on spacing, hierarchy, forms, accessibility and interaction states. The agent audits existing UI against the checklist and outputs a concrete fix list.
features: 100+ actionable interface rules
Element-level audits of existing pages
Covers accessibility and responsiveness
Findings specific enough to fix directly
useCases: Pre-launch UI walkthroughs
Systematically upgrading AI-generated pages
When you'd rather not learn a11y from scratch
skills.bestFor: Teams that want good-UI intuition turned into an executable checklist.
skills.author: Vercel Labs

skills.name: vercel-react-best-practices
skills.tagline: React performance rules wired into your agent's muscle memory
skills.overview: The Vercel team's React / Next.js performance and quality best practices. The agent follows them while generating code — from server-component boundaries to avoiding needless re-renders — like a code reviewer from the React core team on every diff.
features: RSC / client-component boundary decision rules
Patterns against re-renders and request waterfalls
Aligned with official Next.js recommendations
Applies at generation time, not just in after-the-fact review
useCases: Inconsistent quality in AI-written React
Next.js performance work
Unifying frontend code standards across a team
skills.bestFor: Everyone writing React / Next.js with AI.
skills.author: Vercel Labs

skills.name: impeccable
skills.tagline: The polish skill that takes UIs from «works» to «premium»
skills.overview: The most-installed UI-polish skill on skills.sh, targeting the last 5 % between amateur and professional: spacing rhythm, type scales, shadows and radii, alignment, hover-level feedback. It gives the agent a concrete checklist instead of guesswork when asked to «make it look expensive».
features: Checklist-driven visual polish: spacing, type scale, shadow, radius
Token-level consistency — one feel across the whole UI
Interaction details beyond static mockups
Equally useful for new builds and upgrading existing screens
useCases: AI-built UIs that look «almost right» but not premium
The final quality pass before shipping
Acting as the senior designer reviewing an interface
skills.bestFor: Pairs with frontend-design: that one sets the style, this one does the polish.
skills.author: Paul Bakaus

skills.name: interaction-design
skills.tagline: Professional-grade motion and state feedback for interfaces
skills.overview: The interaction-design skill from the huge wshobson/agents catalogue (★40K): timing, easing curves and state feedback defined to professional interaction guidelines — so agents stop slapping on gratuitous transitions and micro-interactions start carrying real information.
features: Duration and easing rules grounded in guidelines, not showreels
Loading, success and failure feedback patterns included
Micro-interactions that prioritise information over decoration
Part of a 100+ role-skill repo — install just what you need
useCases: Buttons and transitions that move but feel off
Missing loading / empty / error states
Raising the overall interaction quality of an app
skills.bestFor: Once the visual style is set, this one fixes motion and feedback.
skills.author: wshobson

skills.name: clone-website
skills.tagline: Give it a URL, get a pixel-perfect Next.js reverse-clone of any site
skills.overview: The core skill of ai-website-cloner-template (★34.7K): not a screenshot-copy but a reverse-engineering pipeline — full-page captures, design-token extraction, an interaction sweep (scroll / click / hover / responsive), then a spec file per component handed to parallel builder agents, finishing with a side-by-side visual diff. Every CSS value must come from getComputedStyle() — no estimating allowed.
features: Pixel-perfect target: colors, spacing, fonts and animation from measured values
Extracts behaviour, not just looks: scroll triggers, multi-state content, hover transitions
A spec file per component before dispatch — builders never guess
Parallel builds in git worktrees, tsc / npm run build verified at every step
useCases: Migrating your own WordPress / Webflow site to a modern Next.js codebase
The site is live but the source is gone or the developer left
Learning how production sites achieve specific layouts and motion
skills.bestFor: Runs best alongside the template's scaffold (Next.js + shadcn/ui) and a browser-automation MCP; installing the skill alone gives you the pipeline itself.
skills.author: JCodesMore

skills.name: Build iOS Apps
skills.tagline: OpenAI's official iOS skill pack: 9 skills for writing, running, debugging and profiling
skills.overview: The most useful iOS entry in the Codex plugin marketplace, shipped from OpenAI's official openai/plugins repo. Note it is a plugin, not a single skill: it bundles 9 standard Agent Skills plus an XcodeBuildMCP config, covering SwiftUI UI work and refactors, App Intents, performance audits, ETTrace captures, leak hunting, simulator debugging and preview mirroring. The plugin manifest itself is Codex-only and installs from Codex's /plugins marketplace, but every skill inside is a normal SKILL.md, so Claude Code, Cursor and the rest can install them individually. You still need macOS and Xcode.
features: 9 skills: ios-app-intents / ios-debugger-agent / ios-simulator-browser / ios-ettrace-performance / ios-memgraph-leaks / swiftui-liquid-glass / swiftui-performance-audit / swiftui-ui-patterns / swiftui-view-refactor
A real build-run-debug loop: the agent compiles, boots the simulator, reads logs and taps the UI instead of only editing code

Focused performance and memory playbooks: symbolicated ETTrace captures, diffed iOS memgraphs, plus SwiftUI rewritten to current iOS 26+ patterns (Liquid Glass included) and thousand-line views split up
The plugin wires XcodeBuildMCP for you; install skills one by one and you have to add that MCP yourself for the debug and simulator ones
useCases: AI writes SwiftUI but can't run it or read simulator errors
The app stutters or its memory keeps climbing and you want profiles and memgraphs to pinpoint why
Migrating old code to Liquid Glass, breaking up huge views, or exposing actions to Siri and Shortcuts
skills.bestFor: iOS/SwiftUI builders who want the agent to compile, run and debug on the simulator rather than just emit code.
skills.platform: Skills are portable (Codex / Claude Code / Cursor etc.); the plugin bundle is Codex-only
skills.author: OpenAI

skills.name: Remotion
skills.tagline: Agents writing video in React — by the official rules
skills.overview: Remotion's official Agent Skills pack: best practices (remotion-best-practices), creation (remotion-create) and rendering (remotion-render) teach the agent to author video as React components the official way and render real files — dodging every classic AI-written Remotion pitfall.
features: Official pack: best practices / create / render end to end
Keeps agents away from common Remotion anti-patterns
Parameterized compositions for batch-generating videos
Produces real video files, CI-renderable
useCases: Product demo videos as code
Data-driven templated videos (swap data each episode)
Treating video as an engineering pipeline, not manual craft
skills.bestFor: People turning video into programmable assets with AI writing Remotion by the book.
skills.pricing: Free & open source (free for individuals/small teams; enterprises need a license)
skills.author: Remotion
